## Summary

This PR now carries only account-local model rejection failover, rebased onto current `origin/main` at `3d23d53f8`.

The output-free overload replay portion that was previously here is already on `main` through the [Soju06/codex-lb#2351](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/2351) lineage (`78e0ecf`, `d8c569e`, `bb9285e`). It was dropped from this branch so the PR does not duplicate landed behavior or manufacture an avoidable merge conflict.

## Behavior

- Exact upstream `model_not_found` is classified as model-scoped and health-neutral. A fresh movable HTTP request may try an eligible sibling account before output is visible; if all candidates reject the model, the original 404 envelope is returned.
- Ordinary `invalid_request_error` behavior is unchanged.
- Pre-created Responses WebSocket `model_not_found` errors use the existing bounded replacement path for movable requests and preserve the original envelope when replacement is exhausted.
- Required owners remain pinned. A proxy-injected continuation anchor is evaluated after fresh-body preparation, so the existing legacy `account_model_unsupported` failover is not disabled on continuation turns. A turn-state owner keeps its original rejection instead of being replaced with an owner-unavailable error.

## Scope

`app/modules/proxy/helpers.py`, the streaming and WebSocket rejection classifiers/replay gates, the `model-scoped-rejection-failover` OpenSpec change, and focused route/foundation tests. No settings, schema, overload carrier, or transport protocol changes.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_failover_foundation.py tests/integration/test_proxy_transient_retry.py tests/integration/test_proxy_websocket_responses.py -q` — **314 passed**, 1 warning.
- `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` — clean.
- `uv run ty check` — clean.
- `npx @fission-ai/openspec@1.11.0 validate --type change --strict model-scoped-rejection-failover` — valid.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

## Relationships

- [Soju06/codex-lb#2351](https://github.com/Soju06/codex-lb/pull/2351): its overload behavior is already on `main`; no duplicate code is carried here.

## Summary

A new file upload currently returns 502 when the selected account's routed proxy connection is refused before dispatch, even if another eligible account can complete it. The file adapter drops typed transport metadata, and the sanitized error message cannot satisfy the legacy transient-error classifier.

Preserve transport phase and replay eligibility through `FileProxyError` and `ProxyResponseError`, then apply the existing unary failover loop using that typed evidence. Successful file creation remains pinned to the account that completed it. Strict owner-bound finalization, TLS verification failures, ambiguous sends, response-body failures, and process-wide network failures do not cross accounts. Legacy direct-transport classification remains intact.

The review follow-up also prevents operation-level replay after an earlier finalization poll has returned. A late pre-dispatch failure cannot move an already-started finalization to another account; first-poll pre-dispatch failover remains available for unpinned files.

## OpenSpec and scope

The existing pre-visible unary retry requirement is the baseline. Its routed-file requirements and operational context are synced to `openspec/specs/responses-api-compat/`, with the change archived under `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-20-fix-files-routed-connect-failover/`.

The verified late-poll follow-up is archived under `openspec/changes/archive/2026-09-27-guard-file-finalize-poll-replay/`.

No new retry loop, setting, migration, dependency, wire payload, or reservation acquisition is introduced.

## Summary

A hard continuity owner is selected from a pool the caller has already narrowed to that one account. When the owner is serving the bounded transient error backoff, the pool goes empty and the turn dies as `hard_affinity_saturated` or `continuity_owner_unavailable` — even though the account is ACTIVE, is serving other requests normally, and would leave the backoff in seconds.

The backoff fallback in `select_account` exists for exactly this, but both of its clauses are unreachable in a pool of one:

```python
if allow_backoff_fallback and (
    len(in_error_backoff) > 1                      # cannot hold in a pool of one
    or (in_error_backoff and hard_blocked_exists)  # inspects the *other* accounts; there are none
):
```

Both ask "is this pool empty for a reason other than the backoff?" by looking at the other accounts. A narrowed owner pool has none, so the question is unanswerable and the fallback never runs.

This contradicts two rules the codebase already states:

- `openspec/specs/sticky-session-operations/context.md`: *"Local caps, retry exclusions, **transient runtime health**, and budget pressure never authorize legacy hard-owner abandonment."*
- `app/modules/proxy/_load_balancer/overload_backoff.py`: the isolation window drops an account *"only while at least one other candidate remains, so the window can never empty the pool"*, and hard continuity owners are *"never moved by this module"*.

A `hard_owner_pool` flag marks a pool the caller narrowed to a resolved owner, and the fallback admits its sole backed-off candidate. Persisted unavailability (paused, deactivated, rate limited, quota exceeded, expired reauth) is filtered before the fallback and still fails closed. Multi-account pools are unchanged: a partially backed-off pool still selects a healthy sibling.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix:` — bug fix (no behavior change beyond the bug)

Linked issue: none — reporting and fixing together.

## OpenSpec

- [x] Not applicable — bug fix that matches the existing spec

The narrowing sites all preserve owner binding; the change only stops a transient backoff from emptying a pool that has no alternative. `sticky-session-operations` already requires that transient runtime health never abandons a hard owner, and the overload-isolation requirement already states that when no overload-free candidate is selectable "the pinned owner MUST be kept". **Happy to add an OpenSpec change if you would rather have the guarantee written down explicitly for the error-backoff stage as well** — say the word and I will push one.

## Changes

There are four places that narrow the pool to a resolved owner, and each needed the flag separately. They were found one at a time in production: fixing each one promoted the next to be the top failure code.

- `app/core/balancer/logic.py` — `select_account` takes `hard_owner_pool`; the backoff fallback admits the sole candidate when it is set.
- `app/modules/proxy/_load_balancer/sticky_selection.py`
  - the `hard_sticky` branch (narrows to `sticky_existing_account_id`) passes `True`
  - `_select_with_stickiness` threads the flag to its three budget-safe helper calls, set from `required_account_id is not None`
  - the seed-preference and the two pinned-owner retention calls take `allow_backoff_fallback=hard_owner_pool` — declining a *soft* pin so a sibling can serve the turn is correct, declining a hard owner is not
- `app/modules/proxy/_load_balancer/unbound_selection.py` — `_select_from` takes the flag, also from `required_account_id is not None`.

Three `allow_backoff_fallback=False` call sites are deliberately left alone: the burn-first eligibility probe (ranks a multi-account pool), the rate-limit grace retry (a rate limit is persisted unavailability, not transient runtime health), and `_pool_has_available_account_without_backoff` (a whole-pool predicate).

One doc nit while here: the comment above the `unbound_selection.py` call says *"Sticky and continuity selection never reach this path."* `required_account_id` is threaded into `UnboundSelectionRequest` and used to narrow the pool a few lines earlier, so continuity selection does reach it. The comment appears to predate that.

## Test plan

New regressions, each verified to fail with its fix reverted:

- `tests/unit/test_load_balancer.py` — sole backed-off owner admitted; counters not cleared; persisted unavailability still fails closed; multi-account pool still prefers the healthy sibling.
- `tests/unit/test_select_with_stickiness.py` — the same through `LoadBalancer._select_with_stickiness`, including the pinned-owner retention path.
- `tests/unit/test_load_balancer_contract.py` — through `balancer.select_account(required_account_id=..., required_continuity_owner=True)`, which is the unbound path.

```
uv run pytest tests/unit -q          # 10275 passed, 97 skipped
uv run pytest tests/integration/test_load_balancer_integration.py \
              tests/integration/test_proxy_sticky_sessions.py \
              tests/integration/test_http_responses_bridge.py \
              tests/integration/test_proxy_responses.py -q    # 387 passed
uv run ruff check app tests && uv run ruff format --check app tests
uv run ty check app
```

(Two pre-existing failure classes on this host, both reproduced on an unmodified checkout of the same base: `test_codex_body_capture_guards.py::test_output_under_a_temporary_filesystem_is_refused` needs unprivileged network namespaces, and the migration tests currently fail on `main` under #2474 — the `MultipleHeads` fork. Neither touches the selection path this PR changes.)

## Production measurements

Deployed on top of `v1.25.0-beta.9` on a 19-account pool during an upstream capacity incident, one commit at a time.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `hard_affinity_saturated` | ~7/min sustained | **0**, for the rest of the day |
| `previous_response_owner_unavailable` | up to 100/min; 13.4% of all requests over 42 min | **0** |

Evidence that this is the backoff and not the other candidates, sampled over 25 minutes before the first commit: 169 blocked selections, all with `excluded_count=0` (not caller exclusions), zero `Account cap exhausted` records (not concurrency caps), two overload-isolation transitions (not the isolation window), across seven distinct owner accounts — always whichever account had just accumulated three transient errors, never a fixed one.

The per-commit progression, each measured live:

1. `hard_affinity_saturated` → 0, and `continuity_owner_unavailable` immediately became the top error code.
2. Bridge owners fixed. The remainder was reported by users as *resume conversations all show "reconnecting"* — a resumed thread arrives as a `follow_up` whose sticky row already names the owner, so it takes the pinned-owner retention path.
3. Pinned-owner path fixed; 120 failures in 120 seconds became 9 in one minute.
4. The last 9-30 were the unbound path. `ACTIVE` account, weekly quota 1%, serving other requests normally, six transient errors in two minutes, then every thread pinned to it died for the length of its backoff.

Client-visible symptoms were HTTP 502, `stream disconnected before completion`, and an endless reconnect loop, since Codex retries roughly once a second and burns its budget against a pool that cannot recover until the backoff expires.

## Summary

A pre-visible rate-limit or quota rejection is already classified for account
failover, but the streaming dispatch wrapper also recorded the rejected account
as the required payload owner. The next selection therefore required and
excluded the same account, surfacing the limit without trying another eligible
account.

This PR prevents that rejected attempt from creating a transient payload owner
only when encrypted content is the body's sole account-scoped retained state.
The exception covers encrypted reasoning and compaction after a coded HTTP 429
or first-event `response.failed` rate-limit/quota rejection. File, container,
vector-store, continuation, turn-state, nonneutral URL, unknown retained input,
and existing dispatch owners remain fail-closed. Code-less burst 429s retain
main's bounded same-account retry behavior.

If the alternate account rejects the retained ciphertext, the proxy emits the
stable `cross_account_encrypted_reasoning_rejected` warning with request,
source-account, target-account, trigger, and upstream-code provenance, without
logging ciphertext. Both literal `invalid_encrypted_content` and the observed
reasoning-decryption rejection shape are recognized, and this request-shaped
rejection does not penalize the target account's health.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix:` — bug fix

Related to #1924. Follow-up context: #1964 and #1965. Overlaps #2069.

Issue #1924's soft prompt-cache affinity theory is not reproducible on current
`main`: excluding that affinity account already permits alternate selection.
#1964 was closed after confirming that, and #1965 was an earlier attempt at the
same mechanism. This PR carries neither PR's `reallocate_sticky` change; it
addresses the distinct dispatch-owner conflict reproduced by retained input,
so it intentionally does not use `Fixes #1924`.

#2069 registers an owner and then moves it by projecting response-owned fields
out of an eligible account-neutral full-resend transcript. This change instead
prevents a rejected pre-visible attempt from registering an owner, and also
covers compacted request bodies that #2069 intentionally rejects. The two
implementations should not land unchanged together.

### Current base dependency

This branch is temporarily rebased on #2461 (`af98e203`) because current
`main` has two Alembic heads. #2461 is CI-green and converges those heads. Once
#2461 merges, this PR can be rebased onto `main` without carrying an unrelated
migration diff.

## OpenSpec

- [x] Includes `openspec/changes/release-previsible-429-payload-owner/`
- [x] Narrows the pre-visible rate-limit/quota exception to ciphertext-only
      account-scoped retained state
- [x] Preserves upstream Codex request and response wire formats
- [x] Specifies the diagnostic and target-account health behavior

## Changes

- Release pending payload ownership only for a classified rate-limit/quota
  rejection when ciphertext is the only account-scoped retained state.
- Keep unresolved files and every other non-ciphertext scoped reference bound
  to the first dispatch account, even without a live durable pin.
- Preserve same-owner handling for ambiguous code-less burst 429s.
- Recognize literal and observed encrypted-content rejection shapes after
  cross-account failover and emit one ciphertext-free provenance warning.
- Treat that request-shaped rejection as account-neutral for target health.
- Cover reasoning and compaction, status and first-event failures, unchanged
  ciphertext, unresolved-file fencing, existing file owners, and the
  no-failover diagnostic control.
